title: Great App, BUT…
body: I use this app daily, and find it very helpful for my ADHD. However, I’m not sure if it’s always done this, or if it needs a bug fix. It gives you audible alarms when you’re half way through a task and nearing/at the end of the task. But recently I’ve noticed it doesn’t make an audible noise reminder when you’ve clicked out of the app and are doing something else on your phone. Developers please can this be changed? As perimenopause is also hitting me and I’m forgetting more and getting more easily distracted from my beloved routines, I am losing track of time without that audible reminder whilst I’m into something else away from the app. Or perhaps it’s a phone setting I need to change? Please help me!
author: LooosyLoo

title: A usable app for ADHDers like me
body: I loved this app, shame I am not able to pay the subscription. I can’t afford it, that’s why the four stars.
author: WinterVeiro

title: Good but needs watch app
body:
It really needs a watch app, i often misplace my phone mid task and then miss the notifications. This is the only thing preventing from signing up.

Also, please have a long press or swipe to edit option on the start routines page too. This would make it much easier to manage a daily schedule. 

The option to custom sort the routines on the ‘manage routines’ page would be super useful and easy to implement too please.
author: Rosgoo

title: Multiple users on 1 account.
body:
I’ve downloaded to try as I have ADHD and my young child shows signs of following suit. I’m hoping this will help with organisation and time management as we are ALWAYS LATE!!! 

I think being able to set up multiple users from 1 account would be great so each user earns their own stars. And Something that would work for family routines where the individuals taking part in the routine may be too young to have their own account but old enough to benefit from the prompt and reward system. Including a family subscription package for multiple users in one household as it is common for ADHD to run in families.
author: Abbygail22

title: It’s a free trail con
body:
It’s is an absolute disgrace, downloaded the app decided it was not for me on the day I downloaded it.. 

knowing that it is a free trial that automatically charges at the end of the free trail.. tried to find where I could “Cancel” the pending subscription, as purchased via the Apple Store I kept getting take to App Store subscription section, where the brill app doesn’t show -  as I have not select the subscription method (monthly/yearly/etc) on selection you are charged. Thus the free trial is a con, as you cannot cancel without making a payment. 

I have now cancelled the subscription within the App Store - I do however notice that with the brill app it till states automatic renewal. 

So disappointed.. would not recommend do not download you will be charged there is no free trial period.
author: shazza122355£

title: I don’t understand why this isn’t more popular
body: I have ADHD so you can be sure I’ve downloaded and tried every app out there. This is the best one by far. It’s simple, flexible, and takes all of the ‘knowing what to do’ and helps you turn it into ‘doing what you know’ with easy steps and a bit of gamification. Love it.
author: blackbirdadhd85

title: Perfect premise BUT useless for ADHD
body: This app was honestly everything my ADHD was looking for but without notifications/alarms before every task, it is another useless app on my phone. A really goddamn shame.
author: HonestlyH0n3st

title: Not sure this is for ADHD.
body:
I find there are some apps claiming to be designed for those with ADHD, perhaps sure that is intention or they’re just capitalising on the interest in this. But then… why is there is a time limited trial on an app designed for people susceptible to “time blindness”?

It just makes me think it’s not really for ADHD. Today - the day I found and installed the app - may not feel like the right time if I feel I’ve got so much else going on including using task managers and existing routine apps. So I start the trial, forget about it, then later find half the limited time is over. This is why I immediately deleted the account.
author: This Latest Review

title: Great but needs watch compatibility
body: I really love this app! I was diagnosed with ADHD recently and find this app so helpful in terms of getting my day to day tasks done. The only problem is that I put my phone down to do a task and then forget about it sometimes or get distracted. If there was a watch app that buzzed on my wrist and I could swipe from there that would be amazing!!
author: Blob735

title: Game changer
body: I’ve had this app for a month now. Even though I sometimes forget to use it when I do, it makes such a difference. I love that I can put in a routine then state when I need to finish so I know when to start. And I love you can rearrange tasks without changing the master routine. It’s brilliant 😉
author: Chuckles780709

title: Sooo much potential, just a couple of glitches!
body: I wanted to start by saying I have ADHD and this app is amazing! I only started using it today and I’ve never had such a productive day. It’s also so simple to set up. Only issue I have is that it crashes regularly if I leave a schedule program running and close the app. When I go back to reopen it, the app crashes and goes back to my Home Screen. I’ve tried closing the app properly by swiping it away but it still crashes - any suggestions?
author: mrgncx123
